implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.__init__ creates self.grid = [[" " for _ in range(3)] for _ in range(3)] and Board._all_lines defines all 8 winning lines for a 3x3 board.
GameController.__init__ creates two Player objects and sets self.current_symbol = "X"; take_turn switches self.current_symbol = "O" if it was "X" else "X" after a successful move.
Board.check_winner iterates over all lines and returns "X" or "O" when a line of identical symbols is found; GameController.take_turn sets game_over and winner_symbol accordingly.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect draw when board is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_full returns True when no cell contains a space; GameController.take_turn checks this after each move and marks game_over with draw=True.
GameController.move_history records tuples (symbol, row, col) on every successful move; GUI._update_history displays this list.

implemented_requirements.requirement: User‑friendly interface (clickable grid, status, move history, new game)
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py defines TicTacToeGUI which builds a 3x3 grid of tkinter Buttons, a status label showing the current player, a Text widget for move history, and a "New Game" button.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends when a player wins or board is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: GameController.take_turn returns game_over flag; GUI._handle_game_over disables the board, shows a messagebox, and highlights the winning line if applicable.

judge.summary: All core requirements for a two‑player tic‑tac‑toe game are present and backed by concrete code. The Board class handles grid state, move validation, win/draw detection. GameController orchestrates turn order, move history, and game‑over logic. Player provides simple name/symbol storage. The Tkinter GUI offers a clickable 3x3 board, status updates, move‑history panel, win highlighting, and a reset button. No missing stubs or placeholder code were found, and the code appears ready to run, giving a high functional completeness and executable likelihood.
